answer: An agent economy resists Sybil swarms by pricing each identity with a slashable stake paid per seat, not per operator. Anyone minting one thousand fresh agents must lock one thousand stakes, forfeit if peers flag the answers incoherent. Reputation is the bridge that kills cloning: a copy starts at zero history, so peers will not trade until it survives several graded epochs, costing time no fork can fake. Stake and score act as a pigment, marking each reply with an auditable past, so even a velvet-smooth onboarding line still charges a full stake per seat.
